stage1.impression: A moody night scene: warm record shelves frame a big saturated-blue recess, and a small acrylic turntable sits on a black gloss desk. The glossy reflection of the turntable is the best thing in it. But the hero takes up less than a fifth of the frame and is the same blue as the flat backdrop behind it, the lower third is a dead black slab, and the repeated record spines and the textureless glowing box read as CG, not a photographed interior.

blocking_9: Cumulus must separate from its background in hue and value: the recess behind it must not be the same saturated blue as the acrylic
The desk front and the lower third must hold detail (not 75% crushed to black)
The turntable must be lit by its own motivated pool of light, with a crisp highlight on the platter and arm, and must fill a larger share of the frame
The recess wall needs a real material (plaster, fabric, wood) with micro-texture and a falloff, not a flat emissive field
The record wall needs variation in light and in spines (no visible repetition), plus atmosphere that gives depth

defects.what: desk front crushed to black: no material, edge or reflection reads, so a third of the frame is dead
recess backdrop is a flat, single-hue cyan-blue field (R about 2) with no texture, so it reads as an emissive CG panel
Cumulus is small (about 200 px of 1200) and tinted the same blue as the backdrop, so its silhouette and colour are lost
the desk lamp's cone lands on the back wall above the turntable rather than on it
record spines repeat with near-identical colours and spacing; the shelves are lit evenly with no falloff
the mixer is a plain grey box with flat matte plastic, which reads as a placeholder
the soffit's underside has black slot lines and a hard, plain edge; the shelf above is cut off awkwardly by the frame
a sliver of the right-hand shelving at the frame edge is a distracting tangent

changes.problem: The recess glows the same saturated blue as Cumulus, so the product disappears into it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 56, r_median 2, g 67, b 110: a monochrome cyan field; the product region's medians (r 5, g 70, b 96) are almost identical

change.to: 0.05, warm neutral (about 3000 K, a dark amber-grey), so the Ice blue acrylic is the only cool element in the recess

changes.expected: The backdrop turns a dark warm grey and the turntable reads as the one blue object, lit through its acrylic

changes.problem: The desk lamp lights the wall above the turntable, not the turntable.

evidence.measured: the wall cone is brighter (lum_median 89) than the product (lum_median 59 in 590,460-800,520)

change.from: 60 W, falling on the back wall
change.to: 90 W, aimed straight down on the platter, beam about 35 degrees with a soft edge, so the pool sits on the desk around Cumulus and grazes the arm

changes.expected: A bright pool on the desk and platter, a crisp highlight on the arm and plinth edge, and the wall falling off darker above

changes.problem: The hero takes up less than a fifth of the frame width and is centred in a sea of backdrop and black desk.

evidence.measured: turntable spans about 200 x 70 px of 1200 x 800

change.to: [16.5, 3.9, 1.30] at the turntable's centre, 45 mm, keeping a vertical strip of the record wall on the left and the soffit's edge just in frame

changes.expected: Cumulus spans about 35-40% of the frame width on the lower third line, with the record wall as context and the desk front reduced to a band

changes.problem: The desk front is a crushed black slab with no material.

change.to: dark smoked oak or satin lacquer with a visible grain, roughness 0.35, so it picks up the warm record wall and the lamp's spill; raise the exposure from 0.5 to 0.7 if needed

changes.expected: The desk front reads as a dark surface with a soft gradient and a lit top edge, not a void

changes.problem: The recess wall is a flat emissive field with no texture, which says render.

evidence.measured: lum_range 46 over the whole field, coming only from the lamp cone; crop shows no micro-detail

change.to: lime plaster or acoustic felt with a fine bump (2-3 mm scale) lit by grazing light from the recess's top edge, so it falls off top to bottom

changes.expected: Visible fine texture and a vertical gradient on the recess wall

changes.problem: The record wall is lit evenly with no falloff, which exposes the repeated spines.

evidence.measured: lum_median 39 with even bands top to bottom; spines repeat in colour and spacing

change.to: top strip 0.5, shelves 0.5, so light rakes down the spines and falls off toward the floor; randomise the spine colour and lean on the shelves (set dressing)

changes.expected: Bright tops of the spines with darker lower shelves; no visible tiling

changes.problem: There is no atmosphere, and the beams and depth read flat.

evidence.measured: the lamp cone has a hard planar shape on the wall with no beam in the air

change.to: volume scatter density 0.004, anisotropy 0.3, in the recess and the room

changes.expected: A faint visible beam from the desk lamp and a softening into the background

changes.problem: The mixer is a plain grey box that reads as a placeholder, and the desk lacks the props that make it a working DJ booth.

evidence.measured: lum_median 26, flat matte surface, no detail

change.to: brushed dark aluminium with a fine anisotropic sheen; add a record sleeve leaning against the recess wall and headphones beside the mixer, kept clear of Cumulus

changes.expected: A believable working booth without competing with the turntable

out_of_scope.request: Cumulus's tint against an Ice blue room: a clear or Fog acrylic Cumulus would read better here
out_of_scope.why: The product's colour is fixed; the change above solves the separation through the room's light instead
